15-112.name: Fundamentals of Programming and Computer Science
15-112.rationale: The description teaches Python programming, program design, testing and debugging.
15-112.course_entry_note: Earn at least C in 15-112 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

15-122.name: Principles of Imperative Computation
15-122.rationale: Imperative programming, correct implementations and basic algorithms/data structures are central.
15-122.course_entry_note: Earn at least C in 15-122 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

15-150.name: Principles of Functional Programming
15-150.rationale: Functional programming, types, recursion and program construction are central.
15-150.course_entry_note: Earn at least C in 15-150 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

15-151.name: Mathematical Foundations for Computer Science
15-151.rationale: Logic, sets, induction, combinatorics and mathematical proof are the explicit focus.
15-151.course_entry_note: The current description restricts enrollment to incoming Computer Science freshmen. Inclusion in this additional-major option does not establish permission for every student. Earn at least C to use 15-151 as a prerequisite for any subsequent Computer Science course.

15-210.name: Parallel and Sequential Data Structures and Algorithms
15-210.rationale: Design, analysis and implementation of parallel/sequential algorithms and data structures are central.
15-210.course_entry_note: Earn at least C in 15-210 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

15-213.name: Introduction to Computer Systems
15-213.rationale: Program execution, storage, communication and systems-level performance are central.

15-251.name: Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science
15-251.rationale: Theoretical computer-science problem solving covers algorithms, complexity, automata and computation.
15-251.course_entry_note: Earn at least C in 15-251 to use it as a prerequisite for subsequent Computer Science coursework.

15-259.name: Probability and Computing
15-259.rationale: The course introduces probability theory motivated by computing applications.

15-386.name: Neural Computation
15-386.rationale: Computational neuroscience seeks to explain biological neurons and natural intelligence, rather than primarily train AI models.

15-387.name: Computational Perception
15-387.rationale: Computational models investigate biological/psychological natural perception; cognitive mechanisms are the central domain.

15-463.name: Computational Photography
15-463.rationale: Optical imaging, graphics, vision and computational photography combine physical-domain and vision methods without a single clear primary category.

15-482.name: Autonomous Agents
15-482.rationale: Integrated autonomous agents use AI reasoning, perception, planning and learning.

15-494.name: Cognitive Robotics: The Future of Robot Toys
15-494.rationale: Robot cognition projects implement perception, recognition, planning and autonomous manipulation.

05-317.name: Design of Artificial Intelligence Products
05-317.rationale: User-centered AI product/service design combines design practice and human interaction; AI use does not establish a primary AI-methods subject.

05-318.name: Human AI Interaction
05-318.rationale: Human agency, ethics and interaction are taught alongside weekly construction of AI systems; neither focus is safely discarded.

05-391.name: Designing Human Centered Software
05-391.rationale: Human-centered interface design, prototyping and user evaluation span software construction and human interaction.
05-391.course_entry_note: This course must be taken synchronously. Undergraduate registration enters a waitlist; HCI minor and SCS concentration students receive stated priority.

11-411.name: Natural Language Processing
11-411.rationale: Language representations, learning, neural models and NLP applications establish AI-method content.

11-441.name: Machine Learning with Graphs
11-441.rationale: Graph neural learning, models and reasoning are explicit methods.

11-442.name: Search Engines
11-442.rationale: Information retrieval models and distributed search architecture combine AI-related retrieval and systems construction.

11-485.name: Introduction to Deep Learning
11-485.rationale: Neural-network theory, architectures, training and implementation establish deep-learning methods.

11-492.name: Speech Technology for Conversational AI
11-492.rationale: Speech recognition, generation and language models support conversational-AI implementation.

10-403.name: Deep Reinforcement Learning & Control
10-403.rationale: Learning autonomous-agent behavior through reinforcement and imitation is central.

10-405.name: Machine Learning with Large Datasets (Undergraduate)
10-405.rationale: Scalable learning methods and parallel/memory/computation infrastructure share the course focus.
10-405.course_entry_note: The description permits an introductory ML co-requisite and asks students taking 10-601 concurrently to inform the instructor; the formal prerequisite expression is retained separately.

10-414.name: Deep Learning Systems: Algorithms and Implementation
10-414.rationale: Building an efficient deep-learning library combines device-level systems, differentiation and AI model design.

10-417.name: Intermediate Deep Learning
10-417.rationale: Supervised and unsupervised deep representations and neural architectures are central.

10-418.name: Machine Learning for Structured Data
10-418.rationale: Structured prediction studies graphical/neural models, inference and learning.

10-422.name: Foundations of Learning, Game Theory, and Their Connections
10-422.rationale: Connections between machine-learning theory and algorithmic game theory give both AI and mathematical foundations substantial scope.

10-423.name: Generative AI
10-423.rationale: Generative/foundation models, training and adaptation establish explicit AI methods.
10-423.course_entry_note: Before registration review the recording policy; attending requires the stated recording authorization agreement. Eligibility or acceptance is not inferred.

10-424.name: Bayesian Methods in Machine Learning
10-424.rationale: Bayesian inference is taught through ML estimation, classification, Gaussian processes and adaptive learning.
10-424.course_entry_note: The description assumes a completed introductory machine-learning course although no formal prerequisite field is given.

10-425.name: Introduction to Convex Optimization
10-425.rationale: Convex optimization properties, duality and numerical methods are central; machine learning motivates the mathematics.

16-161.name: Artificial Intelligence and Humanity
16-161.rationale: Historical, social and ethical interpretations of humanity and intelligent technology are central.

16-350.name: Planning Techniques for Robotics
16-350.rationale: Autonomous robot planning theory and implementations are central.
16-350.course_entry_note: The description expects an introductory robotics course and good knowledge of programming and data structures; no exact prerequisite course code is stated.

16-362.name: Mobile Robot Algorithms Laboratory
16-362.rationale: Robotic autonomy uses sensing, planning and exploration algorithms in progressively developed simulations.
16-362.course_entry_note: The description requires second-year science/engineering mathematics and mastery of an object-oriented language; no exact prerequisite course code is stated.

16-384.name: Robot Kinematics and Dynamics
16-384.rationale: Robot mechanics covers transformations, kinematics, Jacobians and equations of motion; robotics association alone does not make it AI.

16-385.name: Computer Vision
16-385.rationale: Detection, recognition and computational vision/perception are explicit methods.
16-385.course_entry_note: Enrollment is limited to undergraduate students.

16-467.name: Introduction to Human Robot Interaction
16-467.rationale: The course centers human-robot interaction, psychology and design/evaluation of interaction studies; programming is not necessary.
16-467.course_entry_note: The description explicitly states no prerequisites; basic robot familiarity is recommended, and programming is useful rather than necessary.

16-735.name: Ethics and Robotics
16-735.rationale: Robotics/AI are examined through ethics, culture and societal power.

07-280.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning I
07-280.rationale: Search, learning, reinforcement and implementation of landmark AI systems are explicit methods.

07-380.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning II
07-380.rationale: The second AI/ML course extends foundational methods with current AI research topics.

17-200.name: Ethics and Policy Issues in Computing
17-200.rationale: Ethical and policy analysis of computing decisions is central.

21-112.name: Integral Calculus
21-112.rationale: Integration, integral techniques and mathematical applications are the course focus.

21-120.name: Differential and Integral Calculus
21-120.rationale: Differentiation, integration and their mathematical applications are central.

21-122.name: Integration and Approximation
21-122.rationale: Integration, approximation, series and numerical mathematical methods are central.

21-127.name: Concepts of Mathematics
21-127.rationale: Mathematical proof, logic, sets, functions and elementary number theory are central.

21-128.name: Mathematical Concepts and Proofs
21-128.rationale: Mathematical proof, logic, sets, functions and number theory are central.
21-128.course_entry_note: The course is intended for MCS first-semester students interested in mathematical sciences; the description does not establish an unrestricted alternative for every additional-major student.

21-241.name: Matrices and Linear Transformations
21-241.rationale: Linear algebra covers matrices, vector spaces, linear transformations and eigenvalues.
21-241.course_entry_note: 21-127 is strongly recommended; it is not listed as a required prerequisite.

21-325.name: Probability
21-325.rationale: Probability theory, distributions, conditioning and limit theorems are central.
21-325.course_entry_note: The description recommends 21-127 and says it is not an official prerequisite, while the formal field requires one of 15-151, 21-127 or 21-128. Preserve both statements rather than erase the alternative proof-course prerequisite.

21-425.name: Probability and Martingales
21-425.rationale: Rigorous probability and martingale theory are central.

36-218.name: Probability Theory for Computer Scientists
36-218.rationale: Probability foundations and random-process theory support subsequent computing applications.
36-218.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-218.course_entry_note: Statistics majors/minors must complete 36-226. Other students with at least B in 36-218 may enter 36-401 directly; at least C is needed to use 36-218 for the named subsequent Statistics courses.

36-225.name: Introduction to Probability Theory
36-225.rationale: Probability theory covers distributions, conditioning and limit theorems.
36-225.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-225.course_entry_note: Enrollment requires sophomore standing or higher.

36-226.name: Introduction to Statistical Inference
36-226.rationale: Statistical inference includes estimation, testing and regression.
36-226.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-226.course_entry_note: Earn at least C to advance to 36-401, 36-402 or a 36-46x course.

36-235.name: Probability and Statistical Inference I
36-235.rationale: Calculus-based probability and statistical inference are the explicit subject.
36-235.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-235.course_entry_note: Enrollment is currently limited to Statistics primary/additional/dual majors and minors, with sophomore standing or higher and a declaration deadline set by Statistics advisors. Credit for 36-217, 36-218, 36-219, 36-700, 21-325 or 15-259 excludes this course. At least C is required for progression to 36-236, 36-226 or 36-410.

36-236.name: Probability and Statistical Inference II
36-236.rationale: Probability distributions, estimation and multivariate statistical inference are central.
36-236.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-236.course_entry_note: Enrollment is currently limited to Statistics majors/minors and CS majors using the complete 36-235/236 probability sequence. All other students are directed to 36-226. At least C is required to advance to 36-401; the additional-major list does not override the restricted 36-235 entry rule.

36-401.name: Modern Regression
36-401.rationale: Statistical regression and data-model assessment establish the mathematical/statistical subject.
36-401.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses
36-401.course_entry_note: Earn at least C to proceed to 36-402 or a 36-46x course. The description says the spring course is primarily for SCS students, while its offering header lists Fall; these different source contexts are retained without inferring an offering guarantee.

36-402.name: Advanced Methods for Data Analysis
36-402.rationale: Advanced statistical inference and modeling methods are central, despite overlap with predictive learning applications.
36-402.directory_heading: Department of Statistics and Data Science Courses

80-249.name: AI, Society, and Humanity
80-249.rationale: Philosophical understanding, fairness and societal or existential implications of AI are central; technical concepts supply context.

85-110.name: Cognitive Psychology
85-110.rationale: Cognitive psychology studies human memory, language, perception and attention.

85-213.name: Human Information Processing and Artificial Intelligence
85-213.rationale: Human cognitive information processing and AI implementations are explicitly compared and simulated in programming projects.
85-213.course_entry_note: 15-122 or 15-150 may be taken concurrently; concurrent enrollment requires contacting the named course contact for registration.

85-408.name: Visual Cognition
85-408.rationale: Psychological, neural and computational models explain natural visual cognition.

85-413.name: Perception
85-413.rationale: Sensory mechanisms and natural perception are studied through neuroscience and cognitive psychology.

85-421.name: Language and Thought
85-421.rationale: The cognitive abilities supporting natural language learning and processing are central.
